In 2013, X was a 12-year-old with a FIDE rating of 2000 who was one of four children to defeat Magnus Carlsen in a simultaneous exhibition held in Chennai, where Carlsen had come to inspect the venue for his upcoming World Championship match against Viswanathan Anand.

X has since risen to the highest ranks of the chess world and has earned the the 84th Indian Grandmaster title. In 2026, X earned the right to challenge the incumbent for the World Chess title. Who is X?

question_text:
Known by titles such as "The Great", "Lion of the Seas", "The Portuguese Mars" and "Caesar of the East", Alfonso de Albuquerque was the 15th-16th century Portuguese general and second Governor of Portuguese India who established the foundations of the Portuguese colonial empire in the East. He also lends his name to the Alphonso mango, first cultivated by Portuguese Jesuits in coastal regions of Goa and Maharashtra.

As part of his grand plan to control all eastern maritime trade routes, he conquered X in 1507. He thus holds the distinction of being the first European to conquer X, achieving this with just 460 men and 6 ships with powerful artillery against a defending force of 30,000 men and 400 ships.

A figure from Slavic folklore, is described as a ferocious witch who lives in a hut that walks on chicken legs, flies through the air in a mortar wielding a pestle, and kidnaps and eats children.

In the 2019 film Hellboy, this figure appears as a vengeful antagonist who had her eye shot out by Hellboy in 1964, and spends the film plotting to claim one of his eyes in return.

The same figure lends their name as a nickname to another notorious movie character, albeit with an incorrect translation. What is this figure?

X is a coast redwood in California's Redwood National Park, standing at 116 metres, the tallest known living tree on Earth, discovered in 2006 by naturalists Chris Atkins and Michael Taylor.

Named after a Greek Titan, X shares its name with a Hugo Award-winning 1989 sci-fi novel by Dan Simmons, in which a quasi-religious group called the Brotherhood of Y worships nature and travels the galaxy in living treeship spaceships, Y being a direct reference to the 19th century naturalist and conservationist who championed the protection of California's forests and after whom a famous woodland near San Francisco and even a grove in Redwood National Park is named. Identify X and Y.

First documented in a 1968 edition of the Harrow Observer, this management philosophy was later referenced by Tracy Kidder in his Pulitzer Prize-winning book "The Soul of a New Machine" as already "an old expression in corporate America." This management practice effectively cuts off the flow of information from upper management to ground level employees, keeping employees from the real purpose of their work.

In a 2013 Time magazine piece, a former US Navy Secretary highlighted the use of this practice to deal with civilian appointees: "There's an old saying in the Pentagon, we call it the ________ ______, about civilian appointees; you bring them in, keep them in the dark for a year, feed 'em bullshit..." What is this management practice called?

"X Nite Owl Theater", later renamed "X Movie of the Weak" was a comedy show which began its run in 1987. Comprising SNL-style comedy sketches and political satire, it quickly caught national attention across 13 major markets, climbing to #1 in all of them. The show ran for 8 years until it was shut down in 1995 owing to a legal skirmish between two entities of its parent company X.

X was founded on April Fools' Day 1983 in Florida by six entrepreneurs, who borrowed the brand name from an SNL monologue by Steve Martin. Identify X, which is as loud and outrageous as the show it lent its name too.

During filming of the movie X, director Y handed actor Z the script for one of the film's most iconic speeches only on the morning of the shoot, having rewritten it the night before. Unable to memorise it in time, Z printed it out and taped it to his knee. His now-famous downward glance during the scene was him reading his lines.

The speech went on to become not only one of the most iconic lines of cinema but also one of the most widely used memes on the internet. What was this line?
answer_text: One does not simply walk into Mordor!

question_text:
"A Beautiful Mind" is an Oscar-winning biographical drama directed by Ron Howard based on the life of Nobel-winning mathematician John Nash, focusing on his lifelong struggle with mental illness. In one of the early scenes of the movie, John takes a stroll with his roommate Charles, while Charles's niece Marcee plays nearby running through a flock of birds.

What subtle visual clue was planted by the director in the scene that foreshadows the film's central twist about John Nash?
answer_text: The birds don't scatter; Marcee and Charles are hallucinations

Ohlmeyer didn't stop at firing but further retaliated by banning all advertisements for Dirty Work from NBC.

Who are X (7) and Y (3)?

In October 2022, the tabloid the Daily Star began a YouTube livestream of a 60p Tesco X placed next to a portrait of sitting Y, asking the question: "Will she still be ___ _____ within the 10-day life of an X?" The stunt was inspired by an Economist column describing Y as an "_____ lady" with "the life of an X." Seven days later, X won, a hand appeared in frame, slammed Y's portrait face down, "God Save the King" blared, and X, now wearing a blonde wig and a crown, celebrated with a glass of prosecco.

Identify X and Y.

Born in El Paso, Texas and raised in Plano, X had a brief and eventful career as a stand-up comic before quitting after an audience member threatened to kill him. He went on to train at the prestigious Juilliard School, launching a career spanning live-action and voice work. His notable voice roles include Sonny in “I, Robot”, K-2SO in “Rogue One” and “Andor”, Duke Weaselton in “Zootopia”, King Candy in “Wreck-It Ralph”, and Hei Hei, the brainless rooster in Moana.

Since 2012, X has lent his voice to every single Walt Disney Animation Studios feature film, earning a reputation as Disney's unofficial good luck charm. Who is X?

In 1894, Paul D. Hubbard, the deaf quarterback of Gallaudet University — the world's only university for the deaf — was playing a football match against another deaf school. Realising that opposing players who knew American Sign Language could see him signing plays to his teammates near the line of scrimmage and stealing them, he devised a simple solution that went on to become a ubiquitous practice in team sports worldwide and even a fixture of corporate teams. What was this practice?

Hyojonggaeng, literally meaning "dawn bell soup," was a premium version of a Korean soup made with high-end ingredients including short ribs, sea cucumber, and abalone. It was delivered to the homes of high-ranking government ministers on certain mornings in Joseon-era Korea, kept piping hot during cold dawn deliveries by wrapping the heavy pots entirely in thick cotton padding.

Besides being probably one of the earliest instances of ready-to-eat food delivery, the soup also served a critical purpose. What?

Lisa Gherardini was an Italian noblewoman and member of the Gherardini family of Florence and Tuscany. Little is known about her life. Born in Florence, she married in her teens to a cloth and silk merchant who later became a local official; she was a mother to six children and led what is thought to have been a comfortable and ordinary life till the day she died at the age of 63.

While this is a seemingly unremarkable life, Lisa lives on to this day and even has a dedicated mailbox centuries after her passing. How do we better know her?
